messages.subject: NaN read length
parts:
Hello again,

I tried this morning again with a BAM file spanning only the exons of interest and the correspondant BED file.

I think it is more easy for you to give you all the informations, so I attached the .bam, the .bam.bai and the .bed to this mail.

library(CODEX)
bamdir <- list.files(path = "path_of_my_BAM", pattern = '*.bam$', full.names = TRUE)

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: more informations about my problem on CODEX package
parts:
Hello Yvan,


Your codes are all fine and I do see reads mapped to the exonic regions you sent me using samtools. The reason you got 0 reads mapped by getcoverage() and therefore NaN read length is because all of your reads in your bam files are from the second read pair (or maybe it’s single end sequencing). CODEX extracts the first mate pair read and process from there:


  flag <- scanBamFlag(isDuplicate = FALSE, isUnmappedQuery = FALSE, 

                      isFirstMateRead = TRUE)

  param <- ScanBamParam(which = which, what = what, flag = flag)

  bam <- scanBam(bamurl, param = param)[[1]]


I would suggest you check the details of you exon targeted sequencing and the pre-processing of your bam files (mapping etc). This is the first time I’ve seen this issue and the software has been used at UPENN campus quite extensively. Another option for you is to remove the red flag above and re-source your getcoverage() function. You will get reads mapped.



Cheers,

Yuchao

parts:
Hello Xiao,

Please see attached for the latest version of CODEX. The NaN in length and NaN in AIC and BIC problems should be fixed. The package will also be available in Bioconductor tomorrow. Also, if you have case-control data, I suggest you use normalize2() function instead of normalize(), which is also included in the new package. Let me know if you’ve any more questions and thanks for being patient.

Cheers,
Yuchao
